items.title: Kane leaves game for Blackhawks against Avalanche
items.summary: CHICAGO -- Patrick Kane left in the second period with an unspecified injury and did not return for the Chicago Blackhawks against the Colorado Avalanche at United Center on Monday.
items.body: Forward does not return after taking last shift at 14:53 of second period CHICAGO -- Patrick Kane left in the second period with an unspecified injury and did not return for the Chicago Blackhawks against the Colorado Avalanche at United Center on Monday. Kane has nine points (one goal, eight assists) in 14 games, second on the Blackhawks behind captain Connor Bedard with 10 points (four goals, six assists). His eight assists lead the Blackhawks. He’s averaging 18:35 of ice time this season, second among Blackhawks forwards behind Bedard (20:30). The 37-year-old is in his second stint with the Blackhawks after signing a two-year, $16 million contract ($8 million average annual value) with them on June 23. The No. 1 pick by the Blackhawks in the 2007 NHL Draft, Kane helped lead Chicago to the Stanley Cup in 2010, 2013 and 2015. Kane has 1,409 points (509 goals, 900 assists) in 1,383 career games with the Blackhawks, New York Rangers and Detroit Red Wings. He scored his 500th goal on Jan. 8 and broke Mike Modano ’s record for points by a United States-born player with No. 1,375 on Jan. 29. Kane reached 1,400 points on April 13.

Before his recent upper-body ailment, which he suffered in practice, Markström exited Florida’s October 12th matchup against the Buffalo Sabres after the first period. Unfortunately, this isn’t a new theme for the Swedish netminder. Markström battled through multiple injuries last season, his last year with the New Jersey Devils. He’s been limited to seven of the Panthers’ 15 contests this season. He stopped 24 of 28 shots (.857 SV%) in the loss against the Red Wings tonight.

Zuckerberg Cancer Center on Monday with a request for his father, Todd, who was sitting no more than six feet away. “Hey Toddie, make sure you hold those tears in,” the New York Islanders defenseman said. “I don’t want to see that.” Dad tried his best, really he did, but it was understandable a few minutes later when he fought tears while celebrating the opening of the Jennifer Schaefer Child Support Room, an ode to his late wife who died from breast cancer in February 2024. To his credit, Mr. Schaefer held it together for more than a minute when it was his turn to give a speech before he began to discuss the dedicated space -- which came to fruition with the help of a $150,000 donation from the Islanders Children’s Foundation -- that is designed for children while their parents undergo cancer treatment. The hockey-themed room is filled with Islanders memorabilia and provides entertainment including both air and bubble hockey, as well as gaming consoles. “My wife would be so pleased,” Todd said, his voice starting to crack. “… The room is exactly what she would want. items.body: Register Login Islanders Sign Ben Hutton To PTO By Brennan McClain | at November 2, 2026 6:30 pm The New York Islanders have suffered a pair of long-term injuries in their defensive corps this season. First, Alexander Romanov is unlikely to return this season after tearing his ACL in early October. Second, the Islanders recently lost Ryan Pulock for potentially a month with an upper-body injury. Instead of sparingly using some younger options to round out the blue line, New York has opted for a veteran addition. According to a team announcement , the Islanders have signed Ben Hutton to a professional tryout agreement. It’s the second PTO Hutton has signed over the last few months. During preseason, he signed a tryout agreement with the Ottawa Senators. Obviously, that never turned into a standard contract for the 2026-27 season. Now, Hutton hopes that the second time is the charm. Although he’s had difficulty finding a new contract, Hutton is coming off a period of stability. Around this time during the 2021-22 campaign, Hutton signed a one-year deal with the Vegas Golden Knights. Even though he primarily served as a depth defender, Hutton turned a one-year, $750K contract into a five-year stint with the Golden Knights. The former fifth-round pick scored 14 goals and 48 points in 196 games with a +22 rating, averaging 15:21 of ice time per game. He had his name engraved on the Stanley Cup after the 2023 Stanley Cup playoffs. He went scoreless in two games for the Golden Knights en route to their first Stanley Cup championship.

It's a concept that offers plenty of creative freedom and some teams have embraced the opportunity to revisit forgotten designs, while others have leaned into their city's identity. Some have even taken bolder risks with colours and logos. The challenge with alternate jerseys is finding the right balance between paying homage to a team's history and creating something that feels fresh. You want something that supporters will be excited to wear, but you also want a design that looks like it belongs to that particular franchise. items.body: Center has four points in 14 games this season; Seattle receives Wood in return Shane Wright was traded to the Nashville Predators by the Seattle Kraken for Matthew Wood on Sunday. Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. "I was surprised, but I was excited as well," Wright said Monday. "Really unbelievable city and organization. I'm excited to be here. "I think, for me, I always wanted a little more opportunity. I wanted to have more minutes. I wanted to play a bigger role, whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else. I was happy to do that, but I'm moving on from the situation and happy to be here. I'm still young, so I want to hopefully be here for a number of years, build something special here and be part of a winning culture and a winning group." The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. "For us, we just felt it made sense for quite a few reasons," Predators general manager Chris MacFarland said. "We're excited to add Shane. We feel he's a natural fit in the middle of the ice. We feel we've got a great opportunity for him to improve day by day. He'll be a better player in the spring than he is now, and he'll be a better player next fall than he is now. We hope the same for Matthew. This is one that you hope works out for both teams." The Predators (5-4-5) host the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; HHN, CARNHL, SCRIPPS, SN+).

items.summary: Groulx has played sparingly for the blue and white this season and has yet to register a point.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen Brashear-Imagn Images An experienced center is expected to head back to the minors. On Monday, the Toronto Maple Leafs placed forward Bo Groulx on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. If Groulx clears waivers on Tuesday, he can be assigned to the Maple Leafs’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Toronto Marlies. Groulx has been with the Leafs since the onset of the 2026-27 season, but has only played sparingly, having spent most of the first month as a healthy scratch. He was last in the lineup last Thursday, when Toronto fell to the Seattle Kraken , 5-4. In that contest, Groulx logged 6:23 of ice time, putting one shot on goal. In seven appearances thus far, the 26-year-old has yet to register a point. He has a plus/minus of +1 while averaging a hair over eight minutes of ice time per game. The beginning of the new season comes after he played 13 games for the Leafs last year, his first NHL experience in two years, posting three goals and five points. Groulx proved to be a key piece in the Marlies’ success last year. Along with scoring a career-high 28 goals and 52 points in 59 regular-season games, the Rouen, France native posted eight goals and 14 points in 23 playoff contests, helping the Marlies win the franchise’s second Calder Cup . In 85 games in the NHL, Groulx has notched four goals and six assists for 10 points. He’s in the second season of a two-year contract, which he signed with the Leafs in July 2025. The one-way deal carries a cap hit of $812,500. Only one player was put on waivers on Sunday: Washington Capitals defenseman Dylan McIlrath. He cleared on Monday and has been assigned to the Hershey Bears, the Capitals’ primary affiliate.

items.title: Oilers’ Jarry named NHL’s second star along with Thompson and Carlsson
items.summary: Edmonton Oilers goaltender Tristan Jarry has been named the NHL’s second star of the week.
items.body: Edmonton Oilers goaltender Tristan Jarry has been named the NHL's second star of the week. Jarry went 2-0-1, closing the week with back-to-back shutouts to compile a .957 save percentage as the Oilers moved into first place in the Western Conference. He made 25 saves in a 4-3 shootout loss to Detroit last Monday before shutting out the Calgary Flames and New York Islanders in a pair of 4-0 wins. The 31-year-old has gone 4-1-2 with a 2.53 goals-against average and a .901 save percentage on the season. Buffalo Sabres centre Tage Thompson was named the NHL’s first star after leading the league with eight points (five goals, three assists) in three games. He recorded his 10th career hat trick and fourth five-point game in a 7-6 win over Anaheim on Thursday. Anaheim Ducks centre Leo Carlsson was named the third star after tying for the league lead with eight points, including a league-high seven assists. He had back-to-back three-assist games in a loss to Buffalo and a 6-3 win over Ottawa on Sunday.

items.body: Register Login Avalanche Recall Keaton Middleton By Brennan McClain | at November 2, 2026 12:30 pm The Colorado Avalanche have recalled some defensive depth ahead of their upcoming back-to-back contests. According to a team announcement , the Avalanche recalled defenseman Keaton Middleton from the AHL’s Colorado Eagles. Despite the call-up, Middleton is unlikely to play against the Chicago Blackhawks or Columbus Blue Jackets. Still, he could remain on the active roster for the foreseeable future as Colorado’s seventh defenseman. On Thursday, Meghan Angley of Altitude reported that Josh Manson will miss the next two months with an ankle injury. Veteran blue liner Noah Juulsen , who Colorado signed this past offseason, has already moved into the regular rotation with Manson out. Because they have two road games coming up, it makes sense that the Avalanche want additional insurance in case of another injury. It’s a familiar position for Middleton. The 28-year-old Edmonton, AB, native has been with the Avalanche organization since the 2020-21 campaign after a few years with the AHL’s San Jose Barracuda. Since his move East from San Jose, Middleton has primarily played with the Eagles, scoring 15 goals and 74 points in 308 games with a +46 rating. He earned a few opportunities with the Avalanche in the 2020-21 and 2025-26 seasons, but nothing like the 2024-25 campaign. Although it afforded Middleton the most playing time he’s ever received in the NHL, it was a year from Hell for Colorado. The team had so many injuries that they used 43 different players and six different goaltenders throughout the season. Middleton finished the season with two assists in 41 games with a net-zero rating, averaging 11:29 of ice time per game.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Following the shocking announcement that Nikita Kucherov isn’t willing to re-sign with the Tampa Bay Lightning , everyone is wondering what the team’s next move is going to be. The Russian superstar is looking to move on from the only team he has ever known, which pushes the franchise closer to a new era. Yet, as Kucherov is going to stay in the lineup, many are keeping a close eye on general manager Julien BriseBois and what he’s going to do with one of the best playmakers in the NHL. BriseBois has already stated that he has “no intention” of trading Kucherov, meaning this is going to be one last hurrah for the Bolts. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Steven Ellis joined Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton to debate what the Lightning should do for the remainder of the year. Steven Ellis: You’re not going to win a trade involving Nikita Kucherov. We’ve seen that with what happened with the Connor Hellebuyck trade and what’s probably going to happen with the Dylan Larkin trade. items.body: It'll be Sergei Bobrovsky between the pipes on Tuesday for the Toronto Maple Leafs . Despite recent struggles, the prized free-agent addition will start against the Utah Mammoth, head coach Jim Hiller told reporters on Monday. Bobrovsky allowed five goals in his most recent start Thursday against the Seattle Kraken, including the game-winner in the final minute on a shot from the point. On the season, the Russian has a 3-5-2 record with an .885 save percentage and 3.29 goals-against average. He signed a three-year, $21-million deal with Toronto in the off-season. “He does everything possible to give himself the chance to be set up perfectly for the game," Hiller said of Bobrovsky’s routine. items.body: Cammi Granato played with Cindy Curley for the United States women's hockey team in 1990, when they won silver at the inaugural IIHF Women's World Championship. Granato also won gold with the U.S. at the 1998 Nagano Olympics, the first to feature women's hockey, and silver at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics. Granato was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2010, one of the first women to receive that honor, and was assistant general manager for the Vancouver Canucks from 2022-26. Now senior advisor for amateur scouting for the Canucks, Granato shares her thoughts on Curley, who will be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, in a special testimonial. I'm thrilled that Cindy Curley is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. She's the player who I always thought deserved to be in. When she played and was dominating her sport, there wasn't a lot of emphasis on women's hockey in the U.S. I learned about her by happenstance. I played hockey with the boys in Chicago until I was 17 and thought it may be the end of the road for me in hockey because the boys were turning into men. My mom was trying to get me into other sports, knowing that there wasn’t much room for me in men's hockey, and because we didn't know there was women's hockey out east. A father on one of the boys' teams that we were playing gave my mom a pamphlet from Providence College where Cindy was playing. The 62-year-old who grew up in Stow, Massachusetts, just outside of Boston, loves all the things that hockey brought her, not vice versa. "I never thought hockey owed me anything," she said. "I feel like it'll take me the rest of my life to pay back hockey for all the great opportunities and memories. It's a little surreal, honestly." Curley was one of the pioneers of the women's game, a forward who was part of those first world championship teams from the unofficial tournament in 1987 to the IIHF-sanctioned ones in the 1990s. It's why she is being inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto on Nov. 9. Curley won silver with the United States at the IIHF Women's World Championship in 1990, 1992 and 1994. items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid start to the season just keeps going. The Edmonton Oilers captain made NHL history on Sunday night, becoming the fastest player ever to hit 30 assists in a season. McDavid earned his 30th helper on Evan Bouchard's second-period power-play goal against the New York Rangers on Sunday night, hitting the milestone in just 15 games. Wayne Gretzky held the previous record, earning his 30th assist in his 16th game during the 1984-85 season. McDavid has earned at least one assist in all of the Oilers' games so far this season — a feat that broke an NHL record on Thursday with his 13th consecutive game with an assist. He's now up to 15 consecutive games. It's not just the helpers that are coming for McDavid — he's also been piling on the goals. In 15 games, the three-time Hart Trophy winner has nine goals and 39 points, on pace for 218 points over an 84-game season. items.title: Connor McDavid has goal and assist to lead Oilers past Rangers
items.body: NEW YORK — Connor McDavid scored a goal and extended his NHL record season-opening assists streak to 15 games, powering the Edmonton Oilers past the New York Rangers 4-1 on Sunday. On his first shift, McDavid added to his highlight reel and showed why he is widely considered the best hockey player in the world. He banked the puck off the boards to himself, shifted into another gear, blew past defenceman Vladislav Gavrikov and beat Dylan Garand. The goal 50 seconds in broke a tie with two Hall of Famers: the 418th of his career passed Glenn Anderson for the fourth most in franchise history, and his eighth in the first minute of a game put him past Mark Messier for the most with the Oilers. McDavid is the fastest player in league history to 30 assists, leads all scorers with 39 points and is on pace to join Wayne Gretzky as the only players to reach 200 in a season. Evan Bouchard had a goal and two assists to join Bobby Orr, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin as the only defencemen with 25-plus points in his first 15 games. Journeyman goaltender Matt Tomkins, making his first start for Edmonton and seventh in the NHL, backstopped the team to its third consecutive victory by making some key saves among his 28. Colton Dach had two goals, including an empty-netter with 39.4 seconds left to seal it. The Oilers are 7-0 on the road. Garand, allowed three goals on 24 shots in his ninth consecutive appearance since Igor Shesterkin went down with a right knee injury. Pavel Dorofeyev scored for the Rangers, who have lost four in a row and six of their past seven after a strong start.

items.title: Travis Konecny scores in return as Flyers beat Mammoth
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Travis Konecny scored a goal and assisted on another in his first game since missing more than three weeks with an injury as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Utah Mammoth 6-3 on Sunday. Konecny, who missed 10 games with a lower-body injury, scored his first goal of the season at 1:06 of the second period, banking a shot off Utah goalie Karel Vejmelka to put Philadelphia up 2-1. He later set up Christian Dvorak for a one-timer from the high slot to extend the lead to 4-1. Konecny also set the tone with his physical play, finishing with four hits. Owen Tippett, who missed the last six games with an upper body injury, also returned to the lineup for Philadelphia. Matvei Michkov scored the Flyers' first goal, snapping a shot past Vejmelka for his 10th of the season. He became the first Flyer to score 10 goals in his first 17 games of a season since Konecny did it in 2023. Dvorak and Noah Cates also finished with a goal and an assist each. Oliver Bonk added a goal for Philadelphia and Dan Vladar made 19 saves as the Flyers snapped a three-game winless streak (0-2-1). Dmitri Simashev scored Utah's first goal, Mikhail Sergachev added a late power-play goal for Utah, and Logan Cooley scored his eighth goal this season with the extra attacker on the ice, before Cole Knuble iced the game for Philadelphia with an empty-net goal. Vejmelka made 15 saves as the Mammoth have alternated wins and losses over their past eight games. Mammoth: Continue their six-game road trip in Toronto on Tuesday night.

items.title: Two early goals lift Wild to win over Capitals
items.body: WASHINGTON — Quinn Hughes and Michael McCarron scored in the first 5:27 for Minnesota, and the Wild held on for a 5-1 victory over the Washington Capitals on Sunday. Justin Sourdif scored the only goal for Washington in the dying seconds of the second period, but the Capitals' three-game winning streak came to an end during this visit by the Central Division-leading Wild. Maxim Shabanov's power-play goal with 2:23 left in the third restored a two-goal margin, and Kirill Kaprizov added an empty-netter for his 500th career point and league-leading 15th goal of the season. With 24.9 seconds left and the goalie back in, Danila Yurov scored one more for Minnesota. Washington had scored at least four goals in five of its previous six games, but the Capitals ran into a stingy Minnesota team and goalie Jesper Wallstedt. The Wild permitted two goals or fewer for the fifth time in six games. Hughes opened the scoring after only 3:42 with his fifth goal of the season. McCarron's shot from the slot made it 2-0. Sourdif deflected the puck past Wallstedt to cut the lead in half. Alex Ovechkin has just one goal in his first 13 games in what he's said will be his final NHL season. Cole Hutson found him on the doorstep with a pass early in the third period, but with the net open, the puck bounced off Ovechkin's skate and he wasn't able to control it. Ovechkin later had a shot from the slot denied by Wallstedt. Alex Tuch stole the puck near the Minnesota net but was stopped by Wallstedt as well. Jordan Kyrou had a six-game point streak snapped for Washington.

items.title: Predators acquire Shane Wright from Kraken for Matthew Wood
items.summary: The Predators and Kraken swap former first-round picks as Wright finally finds a change of scenery.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Nashville Predators and Seattle Kraken will be swapping a couple of young talents, with center Shane Wright going to Nashville and winger Matthew Wood going to Seattle. The trade comes after Wright finding himself in trade rumours for a significant amount of time, as he has yet to live up to the pedigree of a fourth-overall pick with the Kraken. The Predators swing a deal looking to take a gamble on him in hopes that they finally can find a long-term solution to their center depth. Wright has started the season on a slower note, as he has just three goals and one assist for four points in 14 games before the trade. He’s shown flashes of being the player he was originally drafted to be, but up to this point, he hasn’t had a more successful season than his 19-goal, 44-point campaign in 2024-25. Wright is in the final year of his three-year entry-level contract with an $886,666 cap hit, a contract which has lasted five years due to the contract sliding for the first two seasons. He’ll be a restricted free agent at the end of the season. In return for Wright, the Kraken acquire Wood, who has become one of the more intriguing young power forwards in the league. He caught the hockey world’s attention not just with his six-foot-four, 202-pound frame, but also with his rookie campaign, which saw him get 17 goals and 13 assists for 30 points in 71 games. But like Wright, Wood has also had a slower start to the season, with just one goal and two assists for three points in 14 games. If there’s any concern for the Kraken with this trade, it’s that Wood doesn’t end up like the last goal-scoring power forward from the Preds’ system: Tanner Jeannot broke out with a 24-goal rookie season, but has since only scored 27 goals in the five seasons following it.

Wright, 22, was surprisingly taken fourth overall by the Kraken in 2022 after he was widely expected to be the No. 1 overall pick. In five seasons in Seattle, he has struggled to find his footing and has spent lots of time in the AHL. This season, he has three goals and an assist in 14 games played. His best campaign came in 2024-25, when he posted 19 goals and 25 assists for 44 points in 79 games. Wood, 21, was the No. 15 overall pick by the Predators in 2023. In 91 NHL games across three seasons, he has 18 goals and 16 assists for 34 points. This year, he has a goal and two assists in 14 games. “Matthew is a young forward who adds size and an elite shot to our group,” said Kraken GM Jason Botterill in a statement. “He’s a skilled player, with high hockey sense, who demonstrated his offensive potential last season as a rookie in the National Hockey League. We’re thrilled to welcome Matthew to Seattle and excited to see his impact on our team. We thank Shane for his contributions to our organization and the city of Seattle, and we wish him all the best in Nashville.”

items.title: Jets shut out by Hurricanes’ red-hot goalie Pyotr Kochetkov
items.body: RALEIGH, N.C. — Pyotr Kochetkov ’s 26-save shutout gave him 10 straight victories to begin the season, Sean Walker scored two goals, and the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Winnipeg Jets 7-0 on Sunday. Kochetkov became the third goalie in NHL history to start a season at 10-0. Sebastian Aho, Juuso Valimaki, Logan Stankoven, Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi also scored for the Hurricanes, who’ve won four in a row. Stankoven, Seth Jarvis, Nikolaj Ehlers and Shayne Gostisbehere all had two assists. Kochetkov tied Carey Price’s 10-win mark with Montreal from 10 years ago for the second-longest season-opening streak. Only Jack Campbell holds a longer season-beginning mark with 11 consecutive victories for the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2020-21. Kochetkov’s second shutout of the season pushed his career total to 13 in 135 games. The Jets have lost nine games in a row (0-7-2). Stuart Skinner, who made 12 saves, was pulled after allowing the fifth goal. Clay Stevenson stopped 13 shots in relief. Walker’s short-handed goal began the scoring 5:16 into the game. Aho’s power-play tally came during Carolina’s four-goal spree in the first 10 minutes of the second period. Stankoven’s goal at 9:09 of the second period stretched the lead to 5-0. At the time, the Jets had five total shots on goal. It’s Walker’s his first two-goal output in two seasons with the Hurricanes. Jets: Tuesday night at Montreal to end a four-game road trip.

items.body: Register Login Capitals Acquire Remi Poirier From Devils By Brennan McClain | at November 1, 2026 11:45 am The Washington Capitals have acquired some goaltending depth from a division rival. According to a team announcement , the Capitals have acquired netminder Rémi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils for a 2027 seventh-round pick. Poirier, 25, was drafted 185th overall by the Dallas Stars in the 2020 NHL Draft. The Farnham, QC, native was playing with the QMJHL’s Gatineau Olympiques at the time, earning a career record of 62-46-13 with a .902 SV% and 3.06 GAA. The former sixth-round pick joined the professional ranks in the 2023-24 campaign, splitting his time between the AHL’s Texas Stars and the ECHL’s Idaho Steelheads. However, that was the last time Poirier ever played in the ECHL. He became the starting netminder for the AHL Stars last season. He played relatively well, earning a 27-19-8 record with a .912 SV% and 2.61 GAA. Unfortunately, although he’s had promising postseason performances in the past, he struggled throughout the 2026 Calder Cup playoffs. Surprisingly, the Devils claimed Poirier off waivers from the Stars ahead of the 2026-27 season. New Jersey already had Jake Allen and Nico Daws rostered, so the addition of Poirier raised some questions. Despite spending an entire month with the Devils, he never appeared in a game for them and was rarely invited to practice. After New Jersey acquired Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets, Poirier lost any remaining chance that he would suit up for the Devils. Hopefully, for his sake, he’ll have more opportunity with the Capitals. Washington lost third-string netminder Clay Stevenson before the season via waivers, and Poirier will likely be his replacement on the organizational depth chart.

items.body: Register Login Crosby Makes History Saturday In Montreal By Ryan Long | at November 1, 2026 9:26 am Just 2:08 into Saturday’s game in Montreal, Sidney Crosby fed Erik Karlsson for a one-timer that beat Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler . Whether you watched the game live, caught it on a TV at the bar, or checked the score on your phone, it may have looked like a routine night for the Penguins captain, who had done this 1,111 times before. But this assist meant more. Crosby’s 1,112th career assist gave him the most by any player with one franchise in NHL history, passing the record Hall of Famer Ray Bourque set with the Boston Bruins 26 years ago. Karlsson and Sid seem to have some special milestone connection, as the Swedish defenseman netted an overtime game-winner on Crosby’s 1,000th career assist against the Red Wings in April 2024. In his post-game interview, when asked about the milestone, Crosby stated, “I’ve been pretty fortunate to be part of this organization for a really long time. And it’s crazy how fast it goes. But definitely honored to be in that company,” as reported by King Jemison with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette . Crosby added a goal and another assist in the Penguins’ 5-4 loss to Montreal, which moved him into a tie with Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time points list at 1,771. Crosby is now 27 points shy of Ron Francis for fifth in all-time scoring and 22 assists shy of Paul Coffey for sixth in all-time assists. Although he has gotten off to a slow start by his standards, the Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, native still has 10 points in his first 14 games and looked to have a little extra jump on Saturday against the team he grew up cheering for. items.summary: Being stripped of the captaincy is a rare occurrence in the NHL, and this season we saw the Detroit Red Wings take the 'C' off Dylan Larkin's chest. Today, we look at other examples of players losing their captaincy.
items.body: John Hefti-USA TODAY Sports John Hefti-USA TODAY Sports Stripped Of The 'C': A Look Back At NHL Captains Who Lost Their Letter Mira Johal Partner Nov 1, 2026 3:13 PM Published Nov 1, 2026 3:13 PM Being stripped of the captaincy is a rare occurrence in the NHL, and this season we saw the Detroit Red Wings take the 'C' off Dylan Larkin's chest. Today, we look at other examples of players losing their captaincy. Ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season, Dylan Larkin, former Detroit Red Wings captain, got his ‘C’ stripped before reporting to training camp. Larkin requested a trade over the summer after his team missed the playoffs for the 10th consecutive season. While he remains on the team’s roster, Detroit removed the ‘C’ from his chest, and the team is now running without a captain this season. Following the removal of Larkin’s captaincy, let’s look back at some previous names who have lost the ‘C’ throughout NHL history. More Videos Dustin Brown, RW, Los Angeles Kings From 2008 to 2016, Dustin Brown captained the Los Angeles Kings . He led the team to their first two Stanley Cup championships in 2012 and 2014. After his eight-year run as captain, GM Dean Lombardi and coach Darryl Sutter removed Brown’s captaincy. Following their Cup win in 2014, the Kings missed the playoffs the next year and exited in the first round in 2016. Brown’s stats began to decline, as he scored less than 30 points over those two seasons. With management hoping for a general change for the team, they revoked Brown’s captaincy and passed on the ‘C’ to Anze Kopitar. items.summary: VANCOUVER -- Gavin McKenna had his first NHL homecoming Saturday -- or at least the closest thing to it when you're from Whitehorse, Yukon.
items.body: No. 1 pick of 2026 NHL Draft caps first Western Canada road trip with win at Vancouver VANCOUVER -- Gavin McKenna had his first NHL homecoming Saturday -- or at least the closest thing to it when you're from Whitehorse, Yukon. The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, played in front of family and friends, including his parents, when the Toronto Maple Leafs defeated the Vancouver Canucks 4-2 at Rogers Arena, a place he watched games as a kid, even though it was nearly 1,500 miles away from home. "It was cool," McKenna said. "Obviously, a lot of Leaf fans here as well, so to play in front of my family, came to a couple Canucks games growing up, so to play in that barn and play against that team was pretty cool." McKenna's first Western Canada road trip with Toronto already included stops at the Edmonton Oilers, a 7-2 win Oct. 24, where he saw flags representing the Yukon and Tr'ondek Hwech'in First Nation in the stands, and a 5-2 loss at the Calgary Flames two nights later. There was also a first visit to the Seattle Kraken, where the 18-year-old had his first two-goal game in the NHL in Toronto's 5-4 loss at Climate Pledge Arena on Oct. 28, before wrapping up the road trip in Vancouver with a suite full of family and friends wearing No. 92 Maple Leafs jerseys. Toronto (8-6-2) finished the trip 2-2-0 and McKenna had two goals and two assists amid a lot of media attention. items.title: Sunday Overreactions: Lightning, Wild can’t risk losing stars for nothing
items.summary: The Lightning and Wild find themselves in similar positions, needing to decide the best course of action with stars Nikita Kucherov and Quinn Hughes on expiring contracts. Michael Amato explores their conundrum and more in his Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: Last Friday, Connor Hellebuyck was on the move. A little over a year ago, Quinn Hughes was dealt on a Friday. So were Mikko Rantanen and Matthew Tkachuk before him. Now we’ve learned this past Friday that Nikita Kucherov doesn’t intend to re-sign with the Tampa Bay Lightning , and he has requested a trade. That news was nothing short of colossal, and it has the potential to completely reshape the balance of the Atlantic Division and the Eastern Conference. A Kucherov extension was always going to be complicated . He’s an elite player coming off a Hart Trophy in a market that has exploded, but Kucherov is also going to be 34 when this new deal kicks in, and the Lightning are known for trying to get a bargain in contract negotiations. They still don’t have a $10-million player and a Kucherov extension would blow their internal cap out of the water. However, that’s the reality of today’s NHL. There’s no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. If the Lightning won’t give Kucherov what he wants, someone else will next summer, regardless of his age. Now Julien BriseBois finds himself in a similar position to Bill Guerin, having a player unsigned beyond this season who is a critical piece of a Stanley Cup push. items.body: Canadiens goalie won seven games, had .932 save percentage, two shutouts NEW YORK – Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler, who went 7-1-0 with a 1.84 goals-against average, .932 save percentage and two shutouts in eight starts, has been named the NHL’s “Rookie of the Month” for October. Fowler edged Boston Bruins center James Hagens (5-6—11 in 14 GP), Toronto Maple Leafs left wing Gavin McKenna (5-6—11 in 14 GP), San Jose Sharks left wing Ivar Stenberg (3-6—9 in 15 GP) and New York Rangers goaltender Dylan Garand (4-5-1, 2.69 GAA, .899 SV%, 1 SO) for the honor. Fowler matched the NHL record for wins by a rookie goaltender in a single October, previously achieved by Michal Neuvirth (7-3-0 in 11 GP w/ WSH in 2010), Ed Belfour (7-3-0 in 11 GP w/ CHI in 1990) and Jacques Plante (7-3-1 in 11 GP w/ MTL in 1954). He additionally became the third Canadiens rookie since 1985-86 to compile at least seven victories in any calendar month, following Jakub Dobes (7-3-0 in 10 GP in March 2026) and Carey Price (7-3-0 in 10 GP in March 2008). Fowler, who suffered his lone defeat in his season debut (Oct. 8 vs. NSH), also joined Dobes (7-0-0 from March 24 – April 9, 2026) and Price (7-0-0 from March 20 – April 5, 2008) as the third Montreal rookie since 1982-83 to win at least seven straight appearances. The last rookie on any team to post a longer winning streak was Boston’s Jeremy Swayman from Feb. 19 – March 12, 2022 (8-0-0). Fowler yielded one or fewer goals in four of his eight contests, highlighted by shutouts Oct. 10 vs. DET (30 SV) and Oct. 27 at STL (46 SV). items.title: Flames fall to Avalanche after Makar’s four-assist night
items.body: DENVER — Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and an assist, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Calgary Flames 5-2 on Saturday night. Martin Necas and Brock Nelson also scored, and defenceman Cale Makar had four assists for the Avalanche. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves. Colorado has won two in a row against opponents playing on the second night of a back-to-back. The Avalanche defeated New Jersey on Wednesday and faced Calgary’s No. 3 goaltender, Arsenii Sergeev , less than 24 hours after the Flames beat Seattle. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil scored for Calgary. Sergeev made 29 saves in his second career start and first this season. Sergeev was recalled from the AHL when the Flames placed Devin Cooley on the injured list with a lower-body injury. Colorado was not whistled for a penalty, while Calgary took three — two on a double-minor late in the third period. The Avalanche, who lost defenceman Josh Manson for two months after he injured an ankle against the Devils, saw Nelson exit in the second when he took a shot by Makar off the side of his helmet. Nelson, who scored earlier in the period, was able to skate to the bench and down the tunnel. He returned in the third period. Nelson capped a three-goal burst in the first 10 minutes of the second that gave Colorado a 4-0 lead. Farabee scored 1:43 after Nelson’s goal, and Pospisil made it 4-2 when he scored 1:59 into the third. Lehkonen deflected Makar’s shot from the point at 4:09 to make it 5-2. Two of Blackwood's stops came after MacKinnon made it 1-0 late in the first. Blackwood made a sprawling glove save on Matt Coronato with 8.5 seconds left in the period and then stopped Farabee 12 seconds into the second.

items.title: Canadiens’ Evans among veterans stepping up in Suzuki’s absence
items.summary: What Jake Evans has provided in Nick Suzuki’s absence is worth highlighting, especially considering the standard he’s set for his Canadiens teammates. Eric Engels explains how Saturday’s win showcased the impact Montreal’s veterans have made without their captain.
items.body: MONTREAL — Straight stats, no fancy stuff, here’s what Jake Evans has provided the Montreal Canadiens in Nick Suzuki’s five-game absence: two goals, three assists, a plus-11 rating, and a 55.4 per cent face-off efficiency while averaging 17:04 per game. Next-man-up stuff, indeed. Worth highlighting, no doubt. Especially considering Evans normally plays as Montreal's fourth-line centre but has elevated to set the standard for the maturity the young Canadiens are exhibiting night after night without their captain. “It’s like he always makes the right play,” said Chris Kreider after Evans made enough right plays to notch an assist, win 11 of 16 draws, and finish with a plus-4 rating in a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins Saturday. It was Montreal’s fifth straight win since Suzuki went down with a hand injury. They had two-goal leads in the third period in all five games and executed on the details to win all five in regulation thanks to veterans like the 30-year-old Evans setting the example for players like 22-year-old Owen Beck . Phillip Danault , who played his 800 th NHL game Saturday, is another who’s been doing that. He never tried to do too much, because he didn’t have the blazing speed most superstars had. But he had all the intangibles. He made good passes at the right time. He was crafty with his hands — and elusive even — for a 6-foot-2, 235-pound man. He had these little moves that seemed to fool defensemen every time. He thrived in the most dangerous and painful areas. That tells you how smart he is. He’s not going to where the puck is; he’s going to where he knows the puck is going to be. But “Big Walt,” 6-foot-2, 235 pounds, went to the net anyway. “It was borderline abusive, to be honest with you,” he said with a laugh. “If you’re willing to pay the price in those tough areas, at the end of the day, you get results. Michael DiPietro had fought so long and so hard to even get to this point, to gain a foothold in an NHL that had seemed constantly just out of reach, but now, with his first NHL win in the books, his first NHL shutout seemed possible. There it was, he thought. His mom was giving him a helping hand. As DiPietro said later, “Definitely a good, friendly bounce there, and it wasn’t just by happenstance.” Back home, in Amherstburg, Ontario, the idea was much the same. Assunta Fenty-DiPietro, Michael’s stepmom, was going through her usual game routine -- “basically 9,000 heart attacks,” as his dad, Vic, put it -- when she connected those same dots. “She’s like, ‘That’s Rebecca, I know it,’ she says. ‘Not tonight!’” Vic DiPietro said. “She was jumping three feet in the air and the whole nine yards.” It wasn’t until that morning, Oct. 22, that DiPietro had put it all together. He arrived at TD Garden, knowing that he was getting the start that evening against the Nashville Predators, his third of the season. items.body: VANCOUVER – Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Toronto Maple Leafs dropped the Canucks to 3-12-1, which is grotesque and worse than anyone expected even for the start of a National Hockey League rebuild. But they had their goalie out and pressing for a late tying goal, as they did in Thursday’s 3-2 road loss to the San Jose Sharks, and the Canucks didn’t drown at five-on-five against another superstar-driven team. And even though Vancouver’s poor middle period decided the game, the two shots that allowed Toronto to go ahead 3-1 could have been handled better by goalie Leevi Merilainen. After getting outshot in 12 of their first 13 games, which included a 10-game losing streak, the Canucks have now narrowly outshot their opponents in three straight contests. Shots on Saturday were 29-28. It is sobering that these last three games, a 6-5 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday followed by the goalie-out losses against the Sharks and Leafs, probably constitute a “hot streak” at this stage for the NHL’s worst team. But at least there is progress, which was difficult to find through most of October – a month that was Halloween for the Canucks from start to finish. “Getting closer,” coach Manny Malhotra said Saturday night. “It's not close to where we need to be or need to get to, but there is progress there. It's frustrating as we talk about these games after loss after loss, but we do see improvement in different areas of our game. It's just... tough to see those when there's no correlation to wins.” “Obviously, the end result has to change somehow,” Canucks winger Paul Cotter , part of an effective fourth line, told Sportsnet.

items.title: Anderson, Canadiens hold off Penguins for fifth win in row
items.summary: MONTREAL -- Josh Anderson had two goals and an assist, and the Montreal Canadiens held on for their fifth straight win, 5-4 against the Pittsburgh Penguins at Bell Centre on Saturday.

items.title: Maple Leafs talk Kucherov trade possibility after win over Canucks
items.summary: Are the Maple Leafs really a candidate to make a deal for Nikita Kucherov? Some of his former teammates now on the Leafs would love to have Kucherov back on their side.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Darren Raddysh was enjoying a nice breather after Friday’s intense Toronto Maple Leafs practice at University of British Columbia when he was alerted to some big news regarding a longtime teammate. Nikita Kucherov — the Lightning’s all-time leading scorer and reigning NHL MVP — had requested a trade out of Tampa Bay, a dramatic step resulting from a contract negotiation stalemate with GM Julien BriseBois. “I thought maybe it was April Fool’s Day,” Raddysh told Sportsnet.ca Saturday, following a rather necessary 4-2 road win over the Vancouver Canucks. “But, yeah, I know how he is, and I know how Julien is. And if they don’t want to come to something, that’s maybe how it’s going to go. “I wish nothing but the best for both of them, so hopefully, maybe they get something resolved. Or they move on. But we’ll see.” The Elliotte Friedman bombshell of Raddysh’s old power-play pal wanting to move on from the only club he’s played for has rocked the league and sent rival GMs scrambling to see if there is a way to assemble a package and pry the six-time 100-plus-point dynamo out of Florida. “Obviously shocks everyone. Don’t know, really, what’s going on there,” another Bolt-turned-Leaf Nick Paul told us. “I mean, yeah, just was shocked.” BriseBois states that he has no intention to trade his 33-year-old cornerstone. Yet the two sides remain millions apart on an extension. Kucherov’s agent, Dan Milstein, tweeted that it is “ unlikely ” his client will follow the path of Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck and stop suiting up for Tampa.
